client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: During routine patient care, a nurse's hands are not visibly soiled. Which hand-hygiene method does CDC prefer in most clinical situations?

options.B: Wash with soap and water after every patient contact regardless of hand condition
options.C: Wear clean gloves instead of performing hand hygiene
options.D: Rinse the hands with water alone

rationale: CDC states that unless hands are visibly soiled, alcohol-based hand sanitizer is preferred over soap and water in most clinical situations. Soap and water are specifically indicated when hands are visibly soiled and in several other defined circumstances. Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene, and water alone is not an adequate hand-hygiene method. Therefore A is the single best answer.
educational_objective: Use alcohol-based hand sanitizer as the preferred hand-hygiene method for most routine clinical situations when the healthcare worker's hands are not visibly soiled.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
source_locator: Recommendations > 'Know when to use alcohol-based hand sanitizer (ABHS) versus soap and water during routine patient care' > 'When to use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer (ABHS)' and 'When to wash with soap and water'; section 'Know when to wear (and change) gloves'
source_claim_supported: Unless hands are visibly soiled, CDC prefers ABHS over soap and water in most clinical situations; soap and water are used when hands are visibly soiled and in specified circumstances; gloves do not replace hand hygiene.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8 / PDF p.12 and Appendix A printed p.26 / PDF p.30: apply principles of infection prevention, including hand hygiene

correction_summary: Rejected the original exact-duration construct because current CDC healthcare guidance says to rub with soap and water for at least 15 seconds and explicitly notes that other entities recommend 20 seconds and either duration is acceptable. Rebuilt the item around the unambiguous CDC healthcare recommendation that ABHS is preferred in most clinical situations when hands are not visibly soiled.
audit_findings: A directly matches current CDC healthcare guidance. B incorrectly makes soap-and-water use universal; C conflicts with CDC's statement that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene; D is not an accepted hand-hygiene method. The original 20-second-only key was removed because CDC healthcare guidance permits both 15- and 20-second recommendations. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
